answer: Randomized Delay Assignment. Each agent's epoch slot is drawn from a verifiable random function over the prior block hash plus its identity key, so no one can precompute or grind placements. An identity counts as a signal only after completing its assigned slot, and late or duplicate slots fail the bridge check at epoch close. The shale cost: each extra identity needs its own key, delay cycle, and failed-slot risk, making N-fold sybils pay N sequential waits plus forfeited throughput.
